correspondence.finding: The named Lakitusaki River is established in the regional coastal literature, but that name has not been tied to these selected lower-route parts by independently read geographic correspondence. correspondence.component_scope: Final bend and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The IBA account establishes that Lakitusaki River has a mouth in the western James Bay coastal-marsh region. It does not identify the exact selected ending or establish the final selected channel, estuarine passage or its connection to the receiving bay. The modeled sea-terminal classification is not independent proof that the selected endpoint is already open James Bay.

correspondence.component_scope: Named coastal candidate and receiving-region context
correspondence.finding: The IBA Ekwan to Lakitusaki Shores account explicitly places the Lakitusaki mouth at the northern end of a coastal-marsh tract on northwestern James Bay. Kataquapit’s firsthand account independently describes visiting a former Hudson Bay trading post on Lakitusaki River during a journey along the James Bay coast. These facts identify a real named river in the relevant coastal setting, without proving the selected upstream route or actual terminal.
correspondence.candidate_name_role: Named coastal river candidate only; not a confirmed component assignment to the selected geometry.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening and upper northwestward course
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the depicted upper channel, continuing northwest along the course labeled Río Tignamar. The source accounts for the opening and intervening joins at corridor scale; it does not designate a surveyed river source.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Tignamar corridor and eastern tributary settings
correspondence.finding: The selection remains on the connected northward trunk through the Oxa and eastern tributary settings. Belén and Lupica identify separate approaching drainage, not aliases imposed on the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Río Seco junction and southwestward receiving bend
correspondence.finding: Río Seco approaches from the north at the selected bend. The Tignamar approach joins the southwestward receiving channel; the selection does not ascend Seco.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward canyon and westward receiving valley
correspondence.finding: Continuous source linework follows the selected southwestern descent and subsequent westward course. The downstream trunk carries the Río San Jose label. Stored-part boundaries are not hydronym boundaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Azapa valley approaching Arica
correspondence.finding: The selection continues west and northwest along the mapped lower trunk and tributary approaches. No lake or separate basin transfer is needed to connect these parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower-valley transition, Arica urban corridor and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The IGM channel ends before the city crossing. Municipal Image 3.1-12 supplies the continuous urban continuation and Pacific ending; Image 3.2-7 and its prose place the mouth beside Chinchorro beach. The selected ending matches that coastal corridor. The imagery, city context and connected route are used, not a current bank or wet-mouth claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake, reservoir, wetland and managed-passage scope
correspondence.finding: The surface layer shows a small separate eastern waterbody outside the selection. No selected lake or reservoir traversal is depicted. The continuous mapped river and municipal urban corridor suffice without assuming an engineered bypass. These sources do not inventory small irrigation works, prove current flow, or establish a wetland boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen northern opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening and southward then eastward headward connection were examined in the supplied selection. None of the actually read independent sources locates this particular feeder and its entry into the northern lake chain.

Crooked Lake is a discovery lead only, not a confirmed selected component.

correspondence.finding: The operator’s historical notice connects Great Burnt Lake spillway releases with North Salmon River and downstream Round Pond/Long Pond context. The chosen continuous route through the intervening river/lake passages is not individually established by the inspected map material.

correspondence.finding: The sources establish a managed Long Pond/Jeddore headpond system and a powerhouse outlet distinct from the lower Salmon River(East Bay) category. They do not establish the selection’s particular reservoir passage, cross-fragment connection and southwestern continuation at corridor scale. Contiguous stored geometry alone is not source proof.

correspondence.component_scope: lower river and actual stored terminal
correspondence.finding: Salmon River(East Bay) is a documented distinct river category, and the coastal pilot identifies East Bay within Northern Arm of Bay d’Espoir. This supports the lower-corridor candidate, but no permitted inspected corridor map traces all of the selected lower route to its actual stored endpoint. The endpoint is not silently replaced with the powerhouse/tailrace outlet.

correspondence.finding: The pinned selection begins with several short eastward links. No independently read original establishes the actual chosen opening, intervening waterbody passages, or its join into the subsequent northeastern course. The modeled line alone is not evidence of a Curtis River headwater.

correspondence.finding: No usable primary map was inspected for these six selected parts, their joins, or any narrow lake/channel or wetland passages. Discovery of an Ellice Hills geological publication does not establish these through-links.

correspondence.finding: The selected northward bend followed by the eastward sequence remains without independent source correspondence. A regional name lead cannot establish the intervening joins or distinguish a continuous channel from separate lake or wetland passages.

correspondence.finding: No successfully inspected original establishes this lower selected sequence, including the eastward-to-southward turns and connections between consecutive parts. No named lake, natural-river or managed passage is inferred from the source discovery snippets.

correspondence.finding: The selected terminal has a sea class in the supplied model metadata. No permitted original map or route-specific primary prose was inspected that establishes the final selected links, actual waterbody passage, mouth, or relation to the Curtis River discovery lead. The source and rendered terminal are not silently conflated.
